LABEL: continuant
definition: An entity that exists in full at any time in which it exists at all, persists through time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

LABEL: occurrent
definition: An entity that has temporal parts and that happens, unfolds or develops through time.

LABEL: realizable entity
definition: A specifically dependent continuant  that inheres in continuant  entities and are not exhibited in full at every time in which it inheres in an entity or group of entities. The exhibition or actualization of a realizable entity is a particular manifestation, functioning or process that occurs under certain circumstances.

LABEL: role
definition: A realizable entity  the manifestation of which brings about some result or end that is not essential to a continuant  in virtue of the kind of thing that it is but that can be served or participated in by that kind of continuant  in some kinds of natural, social or institutional contexts.

LABEL: material entity
definition: An independent continuant that is spatially extended whose identity is independent of that of other entities and can be maintained through time.

LABEL: living tissue
definition: Unfixed fully hydrated tissue, typically employed to monitor dynamic changes in the living state.

LABEL: eosin
definition: Staining with an aqueous or alcoholic solution of eosin Y,colors eosinophilic structures in various shades of red, pink and orange. The eosinophilic structures are generally composed of intracellular or extracellular protein. The Lewy bodies and Mallory bodies are examples of eosinophilic structures. Most of the cytoplasm is eosinophilic. Red blood cells are stained intensely red.

LABEL: hematoxylin
definition: The staining method involves application of hemalum, which is a complex formed from aluminium ions and oxidized haematoxylin. This colors nuclei of cells (and a few other objects, such as keratohyalin granules) blue. The staining of nuclei by hemalum does not require the presence of DNA and is probably due to binding of the dye-metal complex to arginine-rich basic nucleoproteins such as histones. The mechanism is different from that of nuclear staining by basic (cationic) dyes such as thionine or toluidine blue. Staining by basic dyes is prevented by chemical or enzymatic extraction of nucleic acids. Such extractions do not prevent staining of nuclei by hemalum.

macroscopy
definition: Methods for imaging objects large enough to be observed by the unaided eye

LABEL: microscopy
definition: Methods for forming images of objects too small to be observed with the unaided eye

LABEL: dark-field microscopy
definition: Imaging with rejection of the unscattered illumination (removal of the zero order component of the diffracted wave)

LABEL: polarization microscopy
definition: A form of light microscopy that uses polarized light. Such form can be used to image samples that exibit optical anisotropy.

LABEL: scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
definition: Image is formed by scanning the surface of the specimen with a beam of electrons in a raster pattern

LABEL: atomic force microscopy
definition: The scanning probe is maintained at a fixed distance above the surface e of the specimen by van der Waals forces

LABEL: detergent permeabilized
definition: Membrane permeabilization by the action of ionic or non-ionic detergents

LABEL: solvent permeabilized
definition: Permeabilization due to extraction of lipid from membranes by an organic solvent such as acetone or methanol.

LABEL: saponin permeabilized
definition: Saponin, a detergent-like molecule, preferentially forms holes in membranes that contain cholesterol.

LABEL: recorded image
definition: Methods and devices used for capturing an image of a real object; distinct from images created by artwork

LABEL: portrayed image
definition: Methods and devices used for creating images by some form of artwork, as distinct from capturing images by means of some recording device

LABEL: animation
definition: A form of graphical illustration that changes with time to give a sense of motion or represent dynamic changes in the portrayal.

LABEL: illumination method
definition: Sources and methods for illumination

LABEL: detection method
definition: Media and devices employed for recording the alterations in the illumination that result from its interaction with the sample

LABEL: imaged parameter
definition: The physical property of the specimen that leads to the modifications of the illumination that are recorded in the image.

LABEL: widefield illumination
definition: Illumination that covers the entire field of view of the image-forming lens

LABEL: narrowfield illumination
definition: Illumination restricted to a small portion of the field of view of the imaging lens; often one or more diffraction limited spots

LABEL: pulsed illumination
definition: Illumination that varies with time; often achieved with pulsed lasers for the purpose of generating very-high peak illumination power

LABEL: single point scanning
definition: Illumination by a single spot of light that is scanned across the field of view

LABEL: multiple point scanning
definition: Illumination by multiple points of light simultaneously

LABEL: spinning disk scanning
definition: Scanning by multiple points of light arising from pinholes in a spinning disk that is illuminated by a widefield source

LABEL: array scanning
definition: Multiple points of illumination generated by a fixed array of sources.

LABEL: hollow-cone illumination
definition: Illumination parallel or at small angles to the optical axis is attenuated or blocked by a stop

LABEL: anaxial illumination
definition: Illumination is distributed asymmetrically around the optic axis, typically achieved by a non-circular stop placed below the lower lens element and aperture of the condenser.

LABEL: darkfield illumination
definition: Illumination restricted to angles that exceed the acceptance angle of the image-forming lens

LABEL: Rheinberg illumination
definition: Illumination at angles less than the acceptance angle of the image-forming lens is attenuated by a filter to give a colored background of unscattered light; higher angle illumination may be filtered to give a contrasting color

LABEL: inelastic scattering
definition: A form of particle scattering in which the energy of the scattered particle is different from that of the incident particle (contrary to elastic scattering, where the energy remains the same).

LABEL: fluorescence polarization (polarization angle resolved fluorescence emission)
resolution-enhancing method
definition: Methods for increasing the resolution beyond the classical Abbe diffraction limit

LABEL: Wollaston prism
definition: A birefringent optical element typically used to split polarized illumination into two sets of parallel but displaced rays

LABEL: FIONA (fluorescence imaging with one nanometer accuracy)
PAINT (point accumulation for imaging in nanoscale topography)
saturated structured-illumination microscopy (SSIM)
definition: Structured illumination used at sufficiently high power to cause significant ground-state depletion of the imaged fluorophore, thus allowing for non-linear resolution enhancement

LABEL: scanning probe microscopy
definition: Imaging by means of a physical probe that passes over the sample

LABEL: ANSOM
definition: Aperture-less NSOM.

LABEL: polarized light illumination
definition: An illumination method in which the sample is illuminated by light waves of only one polarization, instead of a mix of waves of various polarizations.

LABEL: polarization-sensitive detection
definition: A detection method that only detects light that has a specific polarization.

LABEL: modified objective lens
definition: Uses an objective with extra components to manipulate the wave front in the plane of the objective aperture.

LABEL: linear method
definition: A computational method that is linear in the mathematical sense, meaning that image intensity is conserved and the data remain suitable for all quantitative analyses

LABEL: non-linear method
definition: Computational method that are mathematically non-linear; image intensity is not conserved, and the data are in general not suitable for quantitative analyses of pixel values

LABEL: light-sheet illumination
definition: Illumination in the form of a thin sheet of light directed perpendicular to the optic axis

LABEL: FLIP
definition: Fluorescence loss in photobleaching; a method of determining whether two populations of fluorophore are in diffusive communication with one another by observing the decrease in brightness of one population when the other population is subjected to continuous photobleaching.

LABEL: FRAP
definition: Fluorescence loss in photobleaching; a method of determining the rate and extent of exchange between a localized population of fluorophore and a non-localized diffusible pool, by observing the rate of recovery of brightness of the localized population after photobleaching.

LABEL: FRET
definition: Fluorescence (or Forster) resonance energy transfer; a method of estimating the distance between two fluorophores by measuring the extent of non-radiative energy transfer between the two. Experimentally, this involves selective excitation of one while observing emission from the other.

LABEL: fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy
definition: A fluorescence microscopy method in which the image contrast is derived from the fluorescence lifetime at each point in a two-dimensional image and not the local concentration and/or intensity of the fluorophore.

LABEL: selective plane illumination fluorescence microscopy
definition: A fluorescence microscopy method where the sample is illuminated from the side in a well-defined volume around the focal plane of the detection optics.

LABEL: coherent Raman anti-Stokes microscopy
definition: A form of microscopy that can detect molecularly specific contrasts based on the vibrational spectra of the sample molecules, by producing and detecting Raman-scattered photons.

LABEL: OCT
definition: Optical coherence tomography; an interferometric method of imaging using back-scattered photons (elastic scattering)

LABEL: secondary_electron imaging
definition: Image created using the electrons generated by ionization of a sample due to inelastic scattering of the primary beam of radiation

LABEL: back-scattered_electron imaging
definition: Imaged formed using electrons undergoing elastic scattering at very high angles, with emission of characteristic X-rays

LABEL: detection of current induced in the specimen
specimen_modifying_illumination
definition: Illumination used for the purpose of inducing some observable change in the specimen during the course of an imaging session. This illumination may or may not be the same as the illumination used for imaging. Typically used in conjunction with live-cell imaging

LABEL: slit-scanning illumination
definition: Illumination in the shape of a thin line that is swept over the field of view

LABEL: slit-scan confocal microscopy
definition: Illumination and detection via a thin slit

LABEL: array-scan confocal microscopy
definition: Fixed array of sources focused to an array of spots that is swept over the specimen in raster fashion

LABEL: visualization of contiguous regions
definition: Methods of visualization that differentiate between different regions or surfaces of the specimen based on contiguity

LABEL: visualization by chemical attribute
definition: Methods of visualization that differentiate regions of the specimen on the basis of their chemical properties

LABEL: shadowing and plating
definition: Visualization by depositing a label on the surface of a specimen uniformly (plating), or from a particular direction so that surface topography becomes visible (shadowing)

LABEL: negative staining
definition: Visualization by exclusion of a stain in which the specimen is immersed; compare with "positive staining.

LABEL: TexasRed
definition: Fluorophore with ex/em 589/615

LABEL: Tetramethyl rhodamine (TRITC)
definition: Fluorophore derivative of rhodamine with ex/em 547/572

LABEL: isolated subcellular component
definition: A fragment of a cell, subcellular organelle, or macromolecular complex.

LABEL: secondary electron generation
definition: Electrons generated by inelastic scattering of other radiation, the primary radiation.

LABEL: critical_point dried specimen
definition: Specimen from which water has been removed by a process that avoids liquid-gas and solid-gas phase transitions.

LABEL: unprocessed raw data
definition: Data as acquired, with no alterations that change the pixel values.

LABEL: lyophilized specimen
definition: Specimen from which water has been removed by evaporation under vacuum at a temperature below freezing.

LABEL: X-Rhodamine
definition: Fluorophore derivative of rhodamine with ex/em 580/605

LABEL: serial block face scanning electron microscopy
definition: A method of reconstructing 3D structure by combining in-situ serial sectioning with scanning EM.

LABEL: Raman scattering
definition: The inelastic scattering of photons caused by interaction with matter.

LABEL: source of contrast
definition: The source of the variation in the imaged parameter across the field of view.

LABEL: form birefringence
definition: An optical anisotropy that is caused by the arrangement of structures with different refractive indexes, on a scale smaller than a wavelength.

LABEL: intrinsic birefringence
definition: An optical anisotropy that is a constant, intrinsic property of the material.

LABEL: stress-induced birefringence
definition: An optical anisotropy that is the result of mechanical stress in an otherwise isotropic material.

LABEL: distribution of a specific nucleic acid sequence
differences in adsorption or binding of stain
boundaries between regions with different refractive index
differences in amount of elastic light scattering
differences in deposition of metal shadow
fluorescence polarization microscopy
definition: A mode of microscopy that detects the rotational motion of fluorophores.

LABEL: evanescent wave microscopy nearfield illumination
definition: A nearfield illumination method that uses evanescent wave microscopy.

LABEL: evanescent wave scattering nearfield illumination
definition: A nearfield illumination method that uses evanescent wave scattering.

LABEL: radiography
definition: An imaging technique that uses high energy electromagnetic radiation, typically X-rays, as a source of illumination.

LABEL: X-ray radiography
definition: Radiography using X-rays

LABEL: X-ray tomography
definition: Tomography using X-ray illumination.

LABEL: tomography
definition: An imaging technique that creates virtual sections through the use of any kind of penetrating wave.

LABEL: computed tomography
definition: Tomography in which virtual sections are taken from multiple angles and the results are processed via tomographic reconstruction software to produce 2 or 3D images.

LABEL: focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy
definition: A method of reconstructing 3D structure by combining focussed ion beam milling to remove sucessive layers from a sample block with scanning EM to image the exposed surface between each milling step.

LABEL: SNAP-tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a protein self-labelled with a SNAP-tag. A SNAP-tag is an engineered version of the mammalian enzyme AGT that can covalently bind O6-benzylguanine-based ligands.

LABEL: HaloTag
definition: A visualization method that detects a protein self-labelled with a HaloTag. A HaloTag is a haloalkane dehydrogenase that can covalently bind a fluorescent synthetic ligand.

LABEL: autofluorescence
definition: A visualization method that detects the natural fluorescence emitted by endogenous biological structures or compounds.

LABEL: chlorophyll autofluorescence
definition: A visualization method that detects the fluorescence emitted by chlorophyll.

LABEL: mTurquoise
definition: A visualization method that detects proteins labeled with the mTurquoise fluorescent protein tag from Aequorea victoria.

LABEL: mScarlet
definition: A visualization method that detects proteins labeled with the mScarlet monomeric red fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: blue fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a blue fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: green fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a green fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: cyan fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a cyan fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: yellow fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a yellow fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: far-red fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a far-red fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: orange fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects an orange fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: red fluorescent protein tag
definition: A visualization method that detects a red fluorescent protein tag.

LABEL: wide-field fluorescence microscopy
definition: A mode of fluorescence microscopy where the entire observed field is illuminated.

LABEL: cryogenic transmission electron microscopy
definition: A form of transmission electron microscopy in which the specimen is maintained in a vitrified state at cryogenic temperature throughout imaging. The specimen is rapidly frozen to preserve its native structure in amorphous ice, avoiding the artefacts associated with chemical fixation, dehydration, and staining. Imaging is performed with the specimen held at cryogenic temperature in a transmission electron microscope.

LABEL: cryogenic electron tomography
definition: A form of electron tomography in which a cryo-preserved specimen is tilted incrementally in a cryogenic transmission electron microscope to acquire a series of two-dimensional projection images (tilt series), which are then computationally aligned and reconstructed into a three-dimensional volume (tomogram).

LABEL: cryogenic scanning electron microscopy
definition: A form of scanning electron microscopy in which the sample is maintained in a vitrified state at cryogenic temperatures throughout imaging. Sample preservation is achieved through rapid freezing, resulting in vitreous ice formation, which captures native structures while avoiding chemical artifacts. Imaging occurs in a scanning electron microscope while the sample is held at cryogenic temperatures.

LABEL: cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy
definition: Cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy is a volumetric imaging technique in which the surface of a biological specimen preserved in its near-native, vitrified state is imaged by a scanning electron microscope, then ablated by a focused ion beam (FIB-SEM) to reveal a new surface, enabling three-dimensional ultrastructural reconstruction of cells and tissues without the artifacts introduced by chemical fixation or resin embedding.

LABEL: optical anisotropy
definition: The property of a material whose refractive index depends on the polarization and propagation direction of light.

LABEL: mNeonGreen
definition: A visualization method that detects proteins labeled with the mNeonGreen fluorescent protein tag from Branchiostoma lanceolatum.

LABEL: Cy3B
definition: A visualization method that detects a probe conjugated to a Cy3B label.

LABEL: HiLyte647
definition: A visualization method that detects a probe conjugated to a HiLyte647 label.

LABEL: SR2200
definition: A visualization method that detects the SR2200 dye, typically used to stain cell walls.

LABEL: photobleaching
definition: A method that images the photobleaching of a fluorophore.

LABEL: phototoxicity
definition: A method that images the phototoxicity of a fluorophore.

LABEL: adherent live cells
definition: A sample preparation method allowing the imaging of adherent living cells.

LABEL: stably transfected cells
definition: A sample preparation method allowing the image of stably transfected cells.

LABEL: molecular_function
definition: A molecular process that can be carried out by the action of a single macromolecular machine, usually via direct physical interactions with other molecular entities. Function in this sense denotes an action, or activity, that a gene product (or a complex) performs.

LABEL: biological_process
definition: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.

LABEL: kinase activity
definition: Catalysis of the transfer of a phosphate group, usually from ATP, to a substrate molecule.

LABEL: data entity
definition: An information content entity that is intended to be one or more truthful statement(s) about something (modulo, e.g., measurement precision or other systematic errors) and is constructed/acquired by a method which reliably tends to produce (approximately) truthful statements.

LABEL: information content entity
definition: A generically dependent continuant that is about some thing.

LABEL: curation status specification
definition: The curation status of the term. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

LABEL: data about an ontology part
definition: Data about an ontology part is a data item about a part of an ontology, for example a term

LABEL: obsolescence reason specification
definition: The reason for which a term has been deprecated. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

LABEL: denotator type
definition: A denotator type indicates how a term should be interpreted from an ontological perspective.

LABEL: quality
definition: A dependent entity that inheres in a bearer by virtue of how the bearer is related to other entities

LABEL: anatomical entity
definition: Biological entity that is either an individual member of a biological species or constitutes the structural organization of an individual member of a biological species.
